title: The Sharp Phase Transition of Tyler's M-Estimator for Robust Subspace Recovery
summary: Robust Subspace Recovery (RSR) aims to identify an underlying d-dimensional subspace from a dataset heavily corrupted by outliers. Complexity-theoretic results establish a threshold for the problem's computational hardness based on the dimension-scaled signal-to-noise ratio (DS-SNR): the problem is SSE-hard when the DS-SNR is strictly less than 1, and solvable via practical algorithms when it is greater than 1 under general position assumptions.
